justification: Changes who is told they are eligible to build. The endpoint resolved its single most consequential input in the claimant's favour whenever it was absent, and the AI path invented four site measurements to force an answer. Over-eligibility is the expensive direction of this error: someone acts on it.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: `inLMRArea = isLMRArea !== false` returns, the router re-hardcodes isLMRArea: true, or any of the invented defaults (zone || 'R2', lotSize || 450, lotWidth || 12) come back. Mutation-verified: restoring the old default plus the router's hardcoded true fails 4 of the 6 tests. Two further HIGH findings were caught by the new blocking Sol gate on this very push and fixed before merge: the three-state input was collapsing back to a two-state `isEligible: false` response (so 'never assessed' and 'confirmed outside' were indistinguishable to any consumer rendering the boolean), and omitting the zone param dropped the zone FILTER entirely, returning other zones' provisions as applicable to this property.

pre_impl.existing_data: Two eligibility implementations exist. services/housing_sepp_eligibility.py computes the LMR gate from the live 776 exclusion layer and fails CONSERVATIVE on any query failure; its own docstring names the TS route's behaviour as 'a silent over-eligibility bug'. The live assessment page supplies isLMRArea from isLMRApplicable(zone, lga), a zone/LGA lookup rather than the exclusion layer, so the two can still disagree — that consolidation stays open.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Expected one defect in the route. Found three, and the two worst were in the AI router, not the route: it hardcoded isLMRArea: true and substituted zone 'R2', lot size 450 and lot width 12 when the real values were missing; and a second handler in the same file returned R2's DCP provisions for any property whose zone was unknown. The tracker entry described only the route.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new endpoint or surface. The full migration onto the Python service is deliberately NOT attempted here — evaluate_eligibility() returns only the gate result, not the numeric-standards fetch the route also performs, so a swap is not mechanical and the live HousingSEPPEligibilityCard depends on the current response shape.

functions.name: handleHousingSeppCheck
functions.input: the property context assembled by the AI assistant for the current address
functions.output: the eligibility response, or a refusal naming which inputs were missing when the property is not fully known
functions.if_none: a missing zone, lot size or lot width now stops the check and says so is not a finding of ineligibility, instead of substituting defaults

values.value: isLMRArea — whether the property sits in a low/mid-rise reform area, the gate the whole eligibility result turns on
values.read_at: request time from the caller; the live page derives it from isLMRApplicable(zone, lga), the AI path no longer supplies it at all
values.if_missing: treated as NOT ASSESSED and the dependent forms report that they cannot be confirmed, rather than defaulting to true and reporting eligible

queries: N/A - no SQL changed; the numeric-standards fetch in the route is untouched.

break_it.scenario: A caller omits isLMRArea and the endpoint reports the property eligible for LMR forms it may not qualify for.
break_it.what_happens: That was the shipped behaviour: `isLMRArea !== false` made undefined mean true. Now only an explicit boolean true opens the gate.
break_it.how: Test asserts the old expression cannot return and that a typeof boolean check guards it.

break_it.scenario: Not-assessed and confirmed-outside read identically, so a user cannot tell a gap from a finding.
break_it.what_happens: Both are ineligible but they are different statements. The unassessed branch now says so and states it is not a finding that the property is outside an LMR area.
break_it.how: lmrAreaKnown selects the wording; asserted by test.

break_it.scenario: The AI answers an eligibility question for a property whose zone, lot size and width are all unknown, using invented values.
break_it.what_happens: It did — zone 'R2', 450 sqm, 12 m, plus a hardcoded in-LMR-area true. Four fabricated site facts feeding a definitive answer. Missing inputs now return a refusal naming them.
break_it.how: Tests assert each default literal is absent and that the refusal wording exists.

break_it.scenario: The AI returns another zone's DCP provisions as though they were this property's.
break_it.what_happens: handleDcpProvisionLookup used zone || 'R2', so an unknown zone silently answered with R2 provisions. The param is now omitted; for-property treats zone as optional and its predicate already admits ALL-tagged provisions.
break_it.how: Checked the route accepts a missing zone before changing the caller rather than assuming it.

break_it.scenario: The response shape changes and the live HousingSEPPEligibilityCard breaks.
break_it.what_happens: No field was added or removed. Only the eligibilityReason string differs, on a branch that already existed and already returned isEligible false.
break_it.how: The live page passes an explicit boolean from isLMRApplicable, so its behaviour is unchanged; only callers that omitted the field are affected, which is the defect.
break_it.repro: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest && npx tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck

break_it.scenario: A test asserts a phrase that spans a TypeScript string concatenation and can never match the source.
break_it.what_happens: It happened twice in this session. The assertion now matches within a single literal.
break_it.how: Comment on the assertion records why the phrase is truncated.

break_it.scenario: The input is three-state but the RESPONSE is two-state, so a consumer renders 'not eligible' for a check that never ran.
break_it.what_happens: Exactly what the first pass shipped. `assessmentStatus: 'eligible' | 'ineligible' | 'not_assessed'` is now returned alongside the unchanged `isEligible`, so existing consumers keep working and new ones can distinguish the states.
break_it.how: Caught by the blocking Sol gate on this push — the fix I had just written contained the same defect class it was fixing. Tests assert the union type and the conditional.

break_it.scenario: Omitting the zone from a zone-dependent DCP lookup returns OTHER zones' provisions as this property's.
break_it.what_happens: My first fix replaced an invented 'R2' with no zone at all, which drops the filter rather than narrowing it — a wider version of the same wrong answer. The handler now refuses when the zone is unknown.
break_it.how: Refusal states it is not a finding that no provisions apply, matching the pattern used elsewhere in this PR.
break_it.repro: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/api/housing-sepp-lmr-default.test.ts -t 'zone is unknown'

break_it.scenario: A DCP lookup runs with a zone but no council, returning another council's provisions for that zone as this property's.
break_it.what_happens: Cross-review's third catch. Zone alone was not sufficient scope. The handler now requires zone AND (lga or formerCouncil), and names whichever is missing.
break_it.how: Explicit guards rather than a collected list, so TypeScript also narrows context.zone at the call site.
break_it.repro: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/api/housing-sepp-lmr-default.test.ts -t 'zone is unknown'

break_it.scenario: A missing station distance is reported as a negative determination rather than an unrun check.
break_it.what_happens: My mechanical patch had stamped assessmentStatus 'ineligible' onto every isEligible:false branch, including the one whose reason says the distance is required. That branch is now 'not_assessed'.
break_it.how: Caught by cross-review; the blanket edit is exactly the kind of change that introduces this.

break_it.scenario: The card keeps rendering isEligible alone, so an unassessed property still shows a grey 'Not Eligible' badge despite the new status.
break_it.what_happens: It would have. HousingSEPPEligibilityCard is the only in-repo consumer and rendered the boolean at four places; it now shows an amber 'Not Assessed' state first. assessmentStatus is optional there, so an older response still type-checks and falls back to the previous two-state rendering.
break_it.how: Fixing the API without the consumer would have left the wrong answer on screen — the point of the change.

post_merge.manual_verify: Ask the assistant a Housing SEPP question for an address whose lot dimensions are unknown and confirm it now says which inputs are missing rather than answering. On the assessment page, confirm the Housing SEPP card is unchanged for a property where isLMRArea is supplied.
